reductions: MixedAdmission uses four starter families and finite equality classes, with a retained exact completed token, distinct native collision and deterministic bridge token. Two writers serialize under the one gate. Resource classes are complete, starter-only and exhausted. Exact physical completed output and complete history validation are boundary predicates established by production runtime checks. The family is one selected starter family per run for both new writers. Existing native/completed/bridge owner classes exercise cross-family collision. This is not two simultaneous distinct writer families.

NativeSelectorMove has one updater and one readonly historical call; original publisher/MixedAdmission establish owner exclusion rather than a full state product. Object/metadata/byte/parent/raw-name equality is represented by exact or foreign identity classes. One old and new selector, five location classes and three attempts. Two process crashes plus an initial exhausted-attempt prefix. Append and file/parent barriers, claim/create/write, swap/archive, old archive observation and move observation are separate actions.

Restart resumes the first outstanding source-defined operation after replay/resync of supported retained rows. It assumes process-crash retained bytes, not power-loss durability. The model represents interrupted unclaimed selector creation; actual runtime tests separately interrupt every supplied physical edge.

Generation and receipt use separate source-ordered create, claim, write, barrier, promotion and settlement steps. Repeated directory/file behavior is a representative-role reduction; exact production graphs and capacity vectors are inspected by runtime checks.
Recorded false locations represent malformed retained output graphs; settlement refuses them unless the explicit location mutant removes that guard. This is no arbitrary filesystem-writer theorem.
Completed return is a safety/enabled-transition statement for supported loaded history. No fairness, infinite completion, unlimited history accessibility or native payload theorem.

Fixed-head historical lookup is omitted from NativeSelectorMove. The interrupted-read invariant captures and checks exact move/archive intent sync, fixed new head, expected old and source identity class, and pending-only fallback or observed relocation. Its action property preserves all modeled ledger/output evidence.

savedPc retains abstract evidence across process death. Generation/receipt prefix creation has no physical object identity variable. This model does not independently prove unknown-inode recovery for generation/receipt creation crashes; that remains an original generated-proof and runtime premise.

M6 removes only fresh validateBeforeSync expectedPriorGeneration. MixedAdmission models its no-starter promise and dedicated expected mutation. The native model physical expected-old guard remains unconditional and has no sensitivity claim for M6. The same eleven configurations now use five mixed counterexamples and three selector counterexamples, with unchanged three positives/eight intentional breaks.

candidate-reserved has no caller expected-old field and always takes matches. The expectation class represents frozen fresh-validation input, not an inter-writer selected-head race. The actual public race and original publisher proof supply that evidence.

P4 assumes a sound pending predicate. requirePendingOrder settlement classification is runtime-checked. The retained569 cross-family digest/request collision wrong success proves this premise can fail in real source. Issue481 corrected-source public regression supplies sensitivity; the bounded model does not prove the classifier implementation.
